questions.q: What would have to be true in six months for you to call this a success?
questions.why: Sets the criteria before the tool sets them for you.
questions.need: Success in six months is written down and agreed with the sponsor
questions.how: Write three outcomes with the sponsor and a date for each
questions.listen: A dated outcome the sponsor would sign; "better visibility" alone means nobody will notice success.
questions.probe: Who would have to agree that it worked, and what would they look at?

questions.q: What happened last time a cloud risk reached production, and who found it?
questions.why: A real incident is the strongest reason to change, and shows who cares.
questions.need: A cloud risk is found by the security team before it reaches production
questions.how: Agree which risks must be caught before deployment, and who sees them first
questions.listen: Found by a customer, an auditor or an attacker means the tool is not where the risk enters.
questions.probe: What would have caught it earlier: a check before deploy, or an alert the day it changed?

questions.q: Where does your full list of cloud accounts live: the bill, the organisation, or someone's spreadsheet?
questions.why: Coverage measured against the platform's own list is always perfect.
questions.need: There is one list of cloud accounts everyone trusts
questions.how: Pull accounts from the organisation and the bill, and reconcile the two
questions.listen: One trusted list; three partial ones means accounts nobody watches.
questions.probe: When did someone last find an account that was on none of the lists?

questions.q: Who creates new accounts, and how long until security hears about one?
questions.why: Accounts made outside the process are the ones nobody connects.
questions.need: Security hears about a new account the day it is created
questions.how: Hook account creation to an automatic connection
questions.listen: Same day is good; "when the bill arrives" means weeks with nothing watched.
questions.probe: Is a new account connected by the same step that creates it, or by a ticket afterwards?

questions.q: Are there accounts that are connected but where you rarely see anything?
questions.why: Connected without inventory looks covered and is not.
questions.need: Every connected account is really seen, not just connected
questions.how: List accounts with little or no inventory and fix their permissions
questions.listen: Connected but quiet usually means missing permissions or a region nobody turned on.
questions.probe: Which of those accounts hold something you would not want exposed?

questions.q: Which capabilities did you buy that nobody has switched on yet, and what stopped them?
questions.why: The answer is usually a person or an approval, not the technology.
questions.need: What was bought is switched on, and what blocked it is known
questions.how: Name the blocker for each capability not in use, with an owner
questions.listen: Bought and off is the cheapest gain there is; ask what blocked it, not whether it matters.
questions.probe: Who would have to say yes to switch it on, and what are they worried about?

questions.q: When the tool finds something critical, who gets it and how do they know it is theirs?
questions.why: Findings without an owner are where risk stays open.
questions.need: Every critical finding reaches a named owner who knows it is theirs
questions.how: Map owners to accounts and route findings to them
questions.listen: A finding that lands in a shared queue is a finding nobody owns.
questions.probe: How would the team that owns that resource hear about it, in the tool they already use?

questions.q: How do you accept a risk today, and does that acceptance ever expire?
questions.why: Acceptances without an end date quietly become permanent.
questions.need: Accepted risks have an owner and an end date
questions.how: Record each acceptance with who accepted it and when it expires
questions.listen: Acceptances with no end date are decisions nobody remembers making.
questions.probe: When did someone last review an accepted risk, and change their mind?

questions.q: Do you see what runs inside workloads, or only how the cloud is configured?
questions.why: Configuration alone misses an attacker already running inside a workload.
questions.need: What runs inside the workloads that matter is seen, not only their configuration
questions.how: Choose the workloads where run-time visibility is worth it, and turn it on there
questions.listen: Configuration only is common; it means a breach in progress looks like a clean estate.
questions.probe: Which workloads hold data or reach the internet, and what would you see if one were taken over?

questions.q: Are infrastructure templates checked before they are deployed, or only after?
questions.why: A risk stopped in the pipeline never reaches production.
questions.need: Templates are checked in the pipeline, and the risky ones do not deploy
questions.how: Add the checks to one pipeline and agree which findings block a deploy
questions.listen: Checks after deploy only means the same mistakes come back with every release.
questions.probe: Who decides which findings block a deploy, and what happens when one does?

questions.q: How long does a critical finding stay open, from found to fixed?
questions.why: Time to fix is what the attacker races against.
questions.need: Critical findings are fixed within an agreed number of days
questions.how: Agree the days per severity with the owning teams, and track them
questions.listen: Days is good; weeks or "we do not measure it" means the list only grows.
questions.probe: Which critical finding has been open longest, and who owns it?

questions.q: Which audit, regulation or customer questionnaire must you answer about the cloud this year?
questions.why: A dated obligation turns the work into a project with a deadline.
questions.need: The cloud evidence the next audit asks for can be produced on demand
questions.how: List the controls the audit asks for and where each one's evidence comes from
questions.listen: A named audit with a date makes this urgent; "none this year" means find another reason.
questions.probe: Who signs the answer, and what did the last one cost in hours?
